title: 28-day alignment activation playbook: all-hands + exec brief (draft)
content:
Purpose: Create a compact, actionable plan for the next 28 days that (a) aligns leadership and teams on priority OKRs, (b) prepares an engaging all-hands that communicates trade-offs and asks, and (c) surfaces exec-level decisions that unblock resource shifts.

Context / why now:
- Post-Series C growth window: need stronger cadence between exec priorities and team-level commitments.
- Several cross-functional projects (private deployment launch, Dedicated capacity sizing, and Console rollout) require synchronized ramp plans.
- Goal: reduce ambiguity, give teams a single source of truth for immediate resource decisions.

Quick timeline (28 days):
- Week 0 (now -> +7 days): finalize OKR slate; brief execs; lock all-hands run-of-show; publish pre-read.
- Week 1 (+8 -> +14): team-level micro-OKR commitments; engineering capacity freeze request; customer success prioritization call.
- Week 2 (+15 -> +21): rehearsal week for all-hands; finalize comms; runway risk gating.
- Week 3 (+22 -> +28): all-hands; exec decision day; publish post-mortem and next steps.

Run-of-show (all-hands week):
- 0:00–0:05 — Welcome + context (CEO overview) — goal: set tone, one-line mission reminder.
  Notes: CEO to call out 3 trade-offs (latency vs cost, hosted vs private adoption, speed vs reliability).
- 0:05–0:20 — Product highlights (Head of Product) — focus on Dedicated capacity announcement and pilot metrics.
  Notes: show perf numbers (p95 latency, cost-per-token delta, dedicated utilization %).
- 0:20–0:35 — Engineering update (CTO/Serving Runtime lead) — capacity plan, SLO changes, known infra risks.
  Notes: request: SRE to commit to two on-call hires for high-traffic windows.
- 0:35–0:45 — Customer & GTM snapshot (Head of CS + Sales Ops) — top 5 accounts, adoption blockers, pricing asks.
- 0:45–0:55 — Ops & finance quick brief (CFO) — burn runway implications and proposed reserve for Dedicated contracts.
- 0:55–1:00 — CEO asks + call to action (3 things teams should do inside 28 days)

Pre-read (to go out 48 hours prior):
- One-pager: 28-day priority map (this doc condensed)
- Draft OKR slate (below)
- Key data points: Dedicated pilot metrics, Hosting latency heatmap, Top 10 customer requests
- Ask: Execs to add 2 high-level bullets of risk & mitigation to the Confluence page within 24 hours

Draft OKR slate (company-level) — draft numbers, please review and propose changes:  
Objective A: Deliver reliable production-grade inference at predictable cost for enterprise customers.
- KR A1: Launch Redwood Dedicated public pilot with 3 paying customers and reach >=80% SLA compliance for p99 request latency within pilot environments.
- KR A2: Reduce median cost-per-token for standard hosting workload by 18% vs baseline (Q1 avg).
- KR A3: Ship automated rollback + canary pipeline in Console for model rollouts to cut mean-time-to-rollback from 45m -> <10m.

Objective B: Improve developer experience and observability to reduce lead time and regression risk.
- KR B1: Console: reach 75% of API customers using the new rollout UI for at least one model rollout.
- KR B2: Implement two high-impact eval suites (generation quality + latency regressions) and detect regressions within 24 hours of deploy.
- KR B3: Decrease mean time to detect (MTTD) high-severity incidents from 28m -> 10m.

Objective C: Scale GTM motions for private and dedicated products to capture enterprise deals.
- KR C1: Convert 6 pilot trials into contract commitments for Dedicated or Private (avg contract >= $75k ARR).
- KR C2: Reduce POC-to-contract time from 90 days -> 45 days for prioritized accounts.
- KR C3: Publish two vertical-specific one-pagers (finserv + healthcare) and secure 3 qualified leads per vertical.

Notes on OKRs: these are intentionally aggressive — we expect teams to break them into team-level micro-OKRs during Week 1. Keep confidence scoring per KR (red/amber/green) next to each KR.

Priority resource asks (for exec review):
- One-time engineering burst: 6 FTE-equivalent for Dedicated pilot integration (4 infra, 2 devx) for 6 weeks.
- SRE: two dedicated on-call hires to maintain latency SLOs for peak traffic windows.
- Growth/BDR: +1 SDR to accelerate POC follow-ups for Dedicated pilots.
- Finance: pre-approved contract reserve of $200k to expedite customer procurement for enterprise pilots.

Communications plan:
- T-minus 48h: Pre-read sent to entire company + exec summary thread in #all-hands-announce.
- T-minus 24h: Leadership sync (30m) — final alignment, speaker notes.
- Day-of: live Slack thread; post all-hands: summary + actions (owner, due-date) published to Confluence.

Decision log (items that need exec sign-off during Week 0):
- D1: Approve the one-time engineering burst and the funding source (Finance to confirm).
- D2: Approve the Dedicated pilot customer list (priority: North America + EU).
- D3: Confirm SLA targets for pilot and fallback policy for hosted customers.

Risk register (top 6):
- Capacity risk: Dedicated pilot could oversubscribe our current GPU pool -> mitigation: prioritized quota, preemptible fallback.
- Quality regression: New rollout UI + canary flow may introduce regressions -> mitigation: gated evals, staged rollout.
- Sales friction: procurement timelines longer than expected -> mitigation: Finance-supported accelerator fund and legal template.
- Observability gap: insufficient traces for model-level debugging -> mitigation: devx sprint to add tracing hooks.
- Customer messaging risk: misaligned expectations about GA timeline -> mitigation: explicit language in comms (pilot vs GA).
- Hiring lag: SRE and infra hires may take 6–10 weeks -> mitigation: contract SMEs and on-call overtime compensation.

Open questions / asks for execs (please answer on this doc or add comments):
- Q1: Finance — can you confirm source for the $200k pilot reserve by EOD +3 days? (PRIORITY)
- Q2: CTO — agree with the 6-FTE burst as scoped? any pushback on reprioritization of platform work?
- Q3: Sales — which 3 pilot customers should be prioritized for dedicated contracts (by ARR potential)?
- Q4: Legal — are there any redlines in the proposed dedicated pilot contract template?

Post mortem / follow-up cadence (after day 28):
- Publish a 1-page post-mortem within 7 days of all-hands covering: decisions made, resource allocations, missed commitments, and next sprint-level plan.
- Weekly 30m alignment check with execs for 6 weeks (owner: Priya) — track confidence per KR.
- Ops: create dashboard tiles for each company KR in Console and set alerts for regressions.

Appendix (supporting artifacts / quick links):
- Pilot metrics snapshot (internal dashboard link) — summary table to be attached before pre-read send.
- Legal pilot template: github.com/redwood-inference/contracts/draft-dedicated-pilot.md
- Known tickets: JIRA-ENG-4521 (canary pipeline), JIRA-ENG-4599 (rollout UI polish), JIRA-SALES-334 (pilot contracting flow)

Quick TODO (owner buckets):
- Priya: finalize exec slide deck + pre-read by +3 days.
- Evan: run the capacity impact model and publish numbers by +5 days.
- Avery: draft comms and speaker notes and own Slack thread.
- Miguel: sync with finance on reserve and share options.
- Lena: coordinate pilot customer outreach and confirm calendar windows.
- Dmitri: assemble the eval suites + ensure gating rules are in place.

Notes to self / rough ideas (brainstorm-y):
- Consider a 2-minute demo of the rollback flow live (risky but high signal).
- Micro-sessions after all-hands for product teams that want deeper breakout Q&A.
- Short pulse survey immediately after all-hands to capture clarity on top 3 asks (1-question + 2 optional).

End — please leave comments inline or add suggestions in the Confluence linked artifact.

Document history:
- 2026-02-20: initial draft (Priya)
- 2026-03-03: added OKR slate + resource asks (Evan, Miguel)
- 2026-03-10: in_review — ready for exec comments
